open-question.question: With the tool as the file's only writer, how does a user clear a stale recommendation to force its regeneration — a `strip` subcommand or a documented hand-edit exception?
open-question.recommendation: The goal gives the tool every deterministic edit to the document and a strip is one it already performs internally — the per-block primitive behind the transitive strip in reconciliation and the dependent-strip on prune — so exposing it is an argparse entry and a test, and in return the user gets an id-validated one-line call in place of an eye-located multi-kilobyte edit on the one file whose escaping and indentation the goal makes tool-internal, the on-disk document stays the tool's own output without a caveat, and the half-deleted block the tool would refuse at every later call cannot arise; one primitive serving the reconciliation walk transitively and the user one block at a time is one behaviour, not two, and dependents stay untouched exactly as the stale-tags-left-alone rule already says; a skill around it is an additive step to take only if the hatch, unexercised in every commit to date, ever becomes routine — which is what breaks the tie against building one now.
open-question.alternative: The tool gains a `strip` subcommand that takes one or more Short Titles beside the milestone location every other subcommand takes and, for each named block, deletes every child between its `<question>` element and its `</open-question>` line — the `<alternative>`, `<applied-principle>`, `<depends-on>`, and `<recommendation>` children — leaving the wrapper and `<question>` intact, touching no dependent and no `<depends-on>` tag that names the block, rejecting an unknown id with the document unchanged, and doing nothing on a block already bare; the user runs it and re-runs `/recommend-all-open-questions`, whose skip rule regenerates the now recommendation-less block. The sole-writer guarantee holds with no exception — the document on disk is always the tool's own output — and the operation is the per-block primitive the tool already needs for the transitive strip in `<depends-on>` reconciliation and the dependent-strip on prune, so exposing it costs an argparse entry, one pytest case, and one sentence in the sweep skill; the caller names an id instead of locating lines by eye in an entity-escaped document (for the coding agent acting on a user's request, one short command in place of an edit whose old text is the block's whole multi-kilobyte child set), a mistyped id fails loudly, and a half-deleted block the tool would refuse at every later call cannot arise. A mutator no skill invokes — its only caller is the user, or the coding agent on the user's behalf, outside any skill — so unlike every other subcommand its invocation is carried by no runtime prose: the caller must know the tool's installed path (on the host whose plugin root is a variable substituted at skill load, the installed tool must first be found) and the milestone directory, all for an escape hatch that none of the 299 commits touching a `requirements.md` in this repository has ever exercised; and the strip lands uncommitted, riding into the next `Recommendation-annotation:` commit exactly as the hand-clear does today.

The tool stays the only writer any skill or agent uses, and the sweep skill's escape-hatch sentence becomes the one documented exception: the user opens `open_questions.xml` and deletes every line between the block's `<question>` line and its `</open-question>` line, which leaves a well-formed document the tool parses and re-renders on its next write — the reading of "sole writer" the plugin already gives the principle store, which `capture-milestone-principle-updates` alone writes yet the user may hand-edit for an urgent fix. Nothing to build, test, or document beyond rewording the sentence the sweep skill already carries and its echoes in the docs; the exception has a precedent in the principle store; and a hand-edit is the one path that still works when the interpreter or the tool itself is unavailable. The exception lands on the one file whose escaping and indentation the goal makes tool-internal, so the user — or the coding agent acting for them — locates the lines by eye instead of naming an id (for the agent, an edit whose old text is the whole multi-kilobyte child set, the very token cost the goal exists to cut); a deletion one line too long leaves a document the tool refuses at every later call with nothing in the tool able to repair it, one line too short leaves the `<recommendation>` in place so the sweep silently skips the block; and "the tool is the file's sole writer" must carry a caveat everywhere it is stated.

The `strip` subcommand of the first option plus a user-facing skill that wraps it — `strip-open-question-recommendation <Short Title>`, say — which resolves `<MILESTONE_DIR>`, invokes the tool, and commits the cleared block path-scoped under its own function-derived subject, the plugin's ordinary way to expose a file-changing user action. The user types a slash command with a Short Title and nothing else — no tool path, no milestone directory, the same on both hosts — and the clear is recorded as its own provenance-marked commit under the skill-layer commit rule instead of riding uncommitted into the next annotation commit. A whole skill — SKILL.md, frontmatter with a 25-word description, a commit subject, a `docs/skill-reference.md` entry, a `CLAUDE.md` pipeline line, a rebuild of both host trees — for an escape hatch never yet exercised, existing solely to run one tool call because the sweep stays argument-free by design; and it splits one regeneration into two commits, the strip and then the sweep's annotation, where the annotation diff alone already records the replacement.

open-question.question: Is the empty document a self-closing root or an open and close tag pair?
open-question.recommendation: The serializer already writes every empty element self-closing, and the root is an element like any other; a second rule for one tag buys a slightly prettier first diff at the cost of a special case in the one place the format is defined.
open-question.alternative: The one rule for an element that holds nothing & needs no body: write it as `<open-questions/>`. One serializer rule covers the root, `<depends-on/>`, and every other empty element alike. The first `add` rewrites the root line instead of inserting between two existing lines.

A two-line `<open-questions>` … `</open-questions>` document with nothing between the tags. Adding or removing the last block is a pure insertion or deletion in the diff. The root becomes the one element the self-closing rule does not cover.
